projects.title: Four systems I built that are still running
projects.subtitle: Open one to see how it's put together and which trade-offs I made.

items.title: Carrosserie Kris
items.abstract: Local body shop website iterated on continuously since 2021 - performance, SEO, and conversion improvements shipped across a four-year client relationship.

business.summary: A long-term retainer relationship, not a one-off build. The site is the shop's primary lead channel: fast, findable on Google, and with contact forms that reliably convert visits into quote requests.
outcomes: Steady inbound quote requests through the website
Client trusts one partner for updates and maintenance

engineering.summary: React frontend with a Node.js backend, styled with Tailwind. The codebase is optimized for Core Web Vitals and kept evergreen through regular dependency and content updates.
decisions: Mobile-first layout system; animations kept off the critical path
Image and asset pipeline tuned for Largest Contentful Paint
Form handling hardened against spam without hurting conversion
Small, boring stack chosen deliberately for long-term maintainability

items.title: Distributed Intrusion Detection and Prevention System
items.abstract: Distributed intrusion detection and prevention for educational networks. An inline edge device captures traffic, a remote server analyzes it, and block rules are enforced locally without slowing the network.

business.summary: Schools get enterprise-grade network protection on commodity hardware. Threats are detected and blocked in real time, while staff see everything on a single live dashboard - no security team required on site.
outcomes: Real-time threat detection and automatic blocking
One dashboard for the whole network - no specialist needed
Runs on a Raspberry Pi: minimal hardware investment

engineering.summary: A Rust capture agent runs inline on a Raspberry Pi, streams packet data to a VPS for Suricata-based analysis, and applies verdicts locally so the hot path never blocks on the network round-trip.
decisions: Rust on the edge: memory-safe packet handling, zero GC pauses inline
Capture and enforcement decoupled from analysis - fail-open by design
Server-side pipeline containerized with Docker for reproducible deploys
Suricata rule engine drives detection; custom layer handles prevention

items.title: Provilion Broodjes
items.abstract: Full-stack lunch ordering platform for a school: students order, parents manage credits, administrators run daily operations - with integrated payment processing.

business.summary: Replaced manual cash handling with a self-service ordering system. Parents top up credits online, orders settle automatically through Stripe, and the kitchen works from one live operations dashboard.
outcomes: Eliminated cash handling and manual order reconciliation
Parents control spending through a prepaid credit system
Admin dashboard turns daily orders into a single prep list

engineering.summary: Next.js and TypeScript end to end, MySQL for persistence, and Stripe webhooks driving payment reconciliation. Role-based access control separates student, parent, and administrator capabilities.
decisions: Webhook-driven payment flow: credit balances only mutate on confirmed events
RBAC enforced at the API layer, not just hidden in the UI
Transactional order writes keep credit ledger and orders consistent
Email notifications decoupled from the request path

items.title: Het Smaakpand (Closed)
items.abstract: Clean, minimal website for a local sandwich shop: menu display, opening hours, mobile-first. Retired when the business closed its doors.

business.summary: A small business got online fast and affordably. The site did one job - show the menu and get people through the door - and did it without ongoing complexity or cost.
outcomes: Menu and hours instantly findable from any phone
No CMS overhead for a shop with a stable menu
Cleanly decommissioned when the business closed

engineering.summary: Static-first delivery with a deliberately minimal footprint. No frameworks where none were needed - fast loads, trivial hosting, and nothing to patch.
decisions: Static delivery: no server runtime, near-zero attack surface
Hand-tuned CSS instead of a framework for a single-page footprint
Sub-second loads on mobile networks as the primary target
Archived with a clean teardown - no orphaned infrastructure

sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: This Privacy Policy explains how Brent Schoenmakers ("I", "me", or "my") collects, uses, and protects your information when you visit this website (www.brentweb.eu).

sections.title: Analytics Data
paragraphs: This website uses a self-hosted analytics setup to collect limited, pseudonymised information about how visitors use the site. This includes:

list.text: Pages visited and time spent on each page
Referral source (how you found this website)

afterList: Analytics are only recorded after you opt in via the cookie banner. The resulting reports are reviewed privately in Metabase and are not exposed on the public website.

sections.title: Contact Forms & Cost Estimator
paragraphs: When you use the contact form or the project cost estimator on this website, I collect:

list.text: Your message, and the project details you provide - budget range and timeline on the business contact form, or scope, timeline, optional company name and notes in the cost estimator

afterList: This information is used solely to respond to your inquiry, is sent via Resend (a transactional email provider) to my inbox and to yours as a confirmation, and is not shared with any other third party. Submissions are rate-limited by IP address to prevent abuse; that rate-limit counter is held only in server memory, is never written to disk, and is discarded automatically after a short period of inactivity. A hidden field on both forms helps detect automated spam submissions and contains no personal data.

sections.title: Cookies
paragraphs: This website uses the following types of cookies:

list.label: Essential Cookies:
list.text: Required for the website to function properly (e.g. theme preferences)

list.label: Preference Cookies:
list.text: Two first-party cookies remember how you like to browse - bw-locale stores your chosen language and bw-path stores whether you entered via the business or engineering route, so returning visits skip the entry page. Neither contains personal data, neither is shared, and both expire after one year.

list.label: Analytics Cookies:
list.text: Consent-gated first-party analytics requests used to understand website usage and improve the experience

afterList: You can control cookies through your browser settings. However, disabling cookies may affect website functionality.

sections.title: Data Security
paragraphs: I implement security measures to protect your information, including:

list.text: HTTPS encryption for all data transmission
Rate limiting on every form that accepts input, to reduce abuse

afterList: However, no method of transmission over the internet is 100% secure, and I cannot guarantee absolute security.

pain.title: What people usually call me about
pain.subtitle: You don't need to know what to ask for. If one of these sounds like your week, I can probably help.

1.problem: The same order gets typed in twice
1.body: An order comes in one way and someone types it in again somewhere else. Every time that happens there's a chance to get it wrong, and it costs someone about an hour a day.
1.fix: One system where it only gets entered once.

2.problem: The site looks fine, but nobody calls
2.body: It shows up when someone searches your company name, and nowhere else. The people looking for what you actually do never find it.
2.fix: A site people can actually find, judged on how many of them get in touch.

3.problem: A spreadsheet is running the business
3.body: It works fine until two people open it at once, or until the one person who understands it goes on holiday.
3.fix: A proper application with one login for everyone.

faq.title: Before you email me
faq.subtitle: The things people usually ask me first.

1.q: What if I don't know what I need?
1.a: That's how most projects start, so it's not a problem. Tell me what's slowing you down in normal language and I'll tell you what it would take. Sometimes the honest answer is that you don't need me, and I'll say that too.

2.q: Do I own what you build?
2.a: Yes. The code, the domain and the hosting account are all in your name. If you ever want to hand it to another developer, nothing is locked and there's nothing to buy back.

3.a: If something I built breaks, I fix it. That's not a new project and I don't bill it as one. Most people keep me on for small changes afterwards anyway.

4.q: Why is this cheaper than an agency?
4.a: There's no sales team, no project manager and no office to pay for. You're paying for the work itself instead of the overhead around it.

5.a: Within a day or two. I'd rather tell you that honestly than promise an instant reply and then miss it.
